title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A/S is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over a base of characteristic p (or over F_p). Write t_A for its Lie algebra (tangent space along the unit section). Following the previous page, ω_A := det(t_A)^{-1} = ∧^g t_A^∨ is the Hodge line bundle.

The Hasse invariant (end of the previous page, named here). Verschiebung V: A^{(p)} → A induces a linear map on Lie algebras, t_A^{(p)} = t_{A^{(p)}} → t_A. Taking determinants gives (det t_A)^{⊗p} → det t_A, that is, a global section
σ_A ∈ Γ(S, (det t_A)^{1-p}) = Γ(S, ω_A^{⊗(p-1)}).
Grothendieck names σ_A the Hasse invariant of A. It is the determinant of the Hasse–Witt map viewed as a modular-form-like section of ω^{p-1}. Its zero locus is exactly the set of s with A_s non-ordinary, since A_s is ordinary iff V is bijective on Lie(A_s), iff the p-rank equals g.

Duality ω_A versus ω_{A*}.
1. Start from the Hodge filtration of first relative de Rham cohomology: 0 → t_A^∨ (= invariant 1-forms) → H^1_dR(A/S) → t_{A*} (= R^1f_*O_A = Lie of the dual) → 0.
2. Take determinants: det t_A^∨ ⊗ det t_{A*} ≅ det H^1_dR.
3. Since H^*_dR(A/S) = ∧^* H^1_dR, we have det H^1_dR = ∧^{2g} H^1_dR ≅ H^{2g}_dR(A/S) ≅ O_S via the trace map.
4. Because dim A* = g, this gives ω_A ⊗ ω_{A*}^{-1} ≅ O_S. So there is a canonical isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*}, and hence ω_A^{p-1} ≅ ω_{A*}^{p-1}.

Grothendieck then asserts, without proof, three things:
- this isomorphism is compatible with the Frobenius (p-)structures;
- it therefore sends σ_A to σ_{A*} (the Hasse invariants of A and its dual coincide);
- on the ordinary locus it induces an isomorphism of rank-one F_p-local systems det((pA)_ét) ≅ det((pA*)_ét).

Interpretation of the last claim. On the previous page ω_A on the ordinary locus is identified with an F_p-structure attached to det((pA*)_ét). Indeed, (A[p])^0 is multiplicative and Cartier dual to (A*[p])_ét, so t_A ≅ (A*[p])_ét^∨ ⊗_{F_p} O_S. Hence ω_A ≅ det((pA*)_ét) ⊗ O_S, and symmetrically ω_{A*} ≅ det((pA)_ét) ⊗ O_S. The trivialization σ of ω^{p-1} is exactly the reduction of structure group to F_p^*. An isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} that respects σ therefore descends to the F_p-forms, which gives the stated isomorphism of étale determinants.

Purpose. This feeds into the next page: the study of the étale and multiplicative parts of T_p(A) for ordinary A, their Cartier-dual relation with A*, and Serre–Tate-type reconstruction of the p-divisible group from the étale parts of A and A*.
errors: The key assertion 'cet isom est compatible avec les p-structures' is stated without proof and is not formal. The determinant isomorphism passes through H^{2g}_dR, on which Frobenius acts by p^g, i.e. by 0 mod p when g ≥ 1. So one cannot simply say 'Frobenius respects det H^1 ≅ O_S'. One needs a finer argument, for example a local block-matrix computation with F and V on the Hodge filtration using FV = VF = 0 and the duality ⟨Fx, y⟩ = ⟨x, Vy⟩^σ, or the Cartier-duality description on the ordinary locus followed by a density/deformation argument. A possible sign or normalization issue in the canonical isomorphism is also unaddressed.
The 'donc on aurait' is fine, but it silently uses dim A* = g and the trace isomorphism H^{2g}_dR(A/S) ≅ O_S, neither of which is justified on the page (both are standard).

ideas.what: Hasse invariant of an abelian scheme as the determinant of Lie(V): t_A^{(p)} → t_A, giving a canonical section of ω_A^{⊗(p-1)} whose zero locus is the non-ordinary locus
ideas.modern_name: Hasse invariant (determinant of the Hasse–Witt matrix) as a section of ω^{p-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hasse, Witt (Hasse–Witt matrix, 1930s); the formulation as a section of ω^{p-1} is usually attributed to Katz (p-adic properties of modular schemes, 1973) for elliptic curves, and is folklore for abelian schemes

ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration on de Rham cohomology of abelian schemes
ideas.where_published: related material in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and the Montréal notes 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} obtained from det of the Hodge filtration and ∧^{2g}H^1_dR ≅ H^{2g}_dR ≅ O_S
ideas.modern_name: Hodge bundle of an abelian scheme equals that of its dual
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (used e.g. in Faltings–Chai and Moret-Bailly)

ideas.what: Compatibility of ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} with Frobenius structures, so that the Hasse invariants of A and A* correspond
ideas.modern_name: Equality of Hasse invariants of A and its dual
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (appears in the literature on Hilbert/Siegel modular varieties mod p, e.g. Goren)

ideas.what: On the ordinary locus, an isomorphism of rank-one F_p-local systems det((pA)_ét) ≅ det((pA*)_ét), deduced from ω_A ≅ det((pA*)_ét) ⊗ O_S and compatibility with σ
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of the étale p-torsion of ordinary A and A* (F_p-form of ω on the ordinary locus, Igusa-type character)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; implicit in Igusa / Katz-style descriptions of ω on the ordinary locus

missed.claim: For an ordinary abelian scheme in characteristic p, without any polarization hypothesis, the canonical determinant isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} respects the Hasse trivializations. It therefore descends to a canonical isomorphism of F_p^*-torsors det((pA)_ét) ≅ det((pA*)_ét). I am not aware of this unpolarized statement being stated explicitly in the literature, though it follows from standard facts.
missed.quote: et dans le cas A ordinaire, induit un isom det(pA)_ét ≃ det(pA*)_ét
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It gives a canonical comparison of the étale-determinant characters of A and A* on the ordinary locus, relevant to Igusa covers and mod-p modular forms of weight 1 for non-principally-polarized families. It is mostly a curiosity, since in practice one has prime-to-p polarizations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page defines the Hasse invariant of an abelian scheme as a section of ω^{p-1} via Lie(V) around 1969, slightly before Katz's 1973 standard reference. It also sketches ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} and the equality of Hasse invariants of A and A*. All of this is now standard folklore. The only slightly less common item is the induced isomorphism of étale determinants det(pA)_ét ≅ det(pA*)_ét, which is asserted without proof. Historically interesting as an early clean formulation, but not something a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'p-structures [?]' is plausibly 'p-structures' meaning the Frobenius/Verschiebung structures, or possibly 'F-structures'. Either way it refers to compatibility with the maps used to define σ.
'DR^1(A/S)' and 'DR^{2g}(A/S)' denote relative de Rham cohomology H^1_dR and H^{2g}_dR. The vertical '≀' under det DR^1 indicates the isomorphism det DR^1 ≅ DR^{2g}.
'ω_A · ω_{A*}^∨ ≃ O_S': the image shows 'ω_A · ω^∨_{A*}', so the transcription is consistent.
